fieldValues.title: How should the automatic cleanup cycle run?
fieldValues.thinking_reached: No option chosen. Raised by the owner on 2026-10-30 after the first full cleanup: 'We need a regular automatic cleanup cycle. When we see work is stale, we should clean up.' The owner calls it not quite dreamtime, probably the same thing at a different level.
fieldValues.tensions:
Options, none chosen:
- A. Schedule 'wt prune' and 'wt stale' on this machine (a timer), removing what is clean and merged and reporting the rest.
- B. A standing housekeeping job in the clerk that runs the sweep on a cadence: prune what is merged, rescue uncommitted work older than N days to a pushed branch, archive scratch files, and put what needs a decision on the desk.
- C. A level of the dream cycle: dreams over the workspace as well as over memory, with the same rule that a dream decides what it can and leaves the rest.
- D. Each agent cleans up after itself at session end (remove its worktree once merged, push or rescue anything uncommitted), with a SessionStart nudge listing what is stale, as srs-context already does for stray writes.
fieldValues.unresolved_questions: What may run unattended: removing merged work is safe; discarding uncommitted changes is not (the 2026-10-30 sweep could not, and should not, do it unasked). How long before uncommitted work counts as stale (a day? a week?), and whether rescue to a branch is always better than asking. Whether one cycle should cover all of the owner's projects or only SemanticOps.
fieldValues.next_action: Run 'scripts/wt stale' daily for a week and note what it finds and what was safe to clean without asking; then choose.
